Noah Kim: Hi! first-week networking snag: installed Okta Gateway on my MacBook Air (M2, macOS 13) and the VPN shows connected, but `ssh ec2-user@10.4.5.6` to the bastion just hangs. traceroute stops at the VPN gateway. Anyone seen this on Apple Silicon?
Rina Gupta: welcome Noah! quick checklist: 1) did the Okta browser MFA prompt complete after install? 2) what does `netstat -nr` show for 10.0/8 or 10.4/16 routes?
Noah Kim: I did MFA earlier. netstat shows `10.0.0.0/8 169.254.10.1 UGSc 0 0 utun2` but traceroute still drops. Ping to 10.4.5.6 gets no reply.
Rina Gupta: two common causes: split-tunnel policy that only proxies certain domains, or macOS PF interfering with the virtual interface on Apple Silicon. Temporary fix: add a host route so traffic goes via the VPN gw: `sudo route -n add -net 10.4.0.0/16 169.254.10.1` then try ssh. If that works, file an infra ticket to check Okta route push.
Noah Kim: added the route and ssh connects! Also had to `ssh-add` my key after unlocking the keychain.
infra-bot: Noah Kim's IAM tag corp-ssh-access is pending. Infra reviewers: approve to enable console SSM access.
okta-bot: Okta Gateway session requires re-auth to push updated route policies. Noah Kim, please complete the browser MFA when convenient.
Rina Gupta: we'll update the New Hire checklist: after Okta install, complete browser MFA and verify corp routes; if bastion unreachable add the temporary route or restart Okta agent. Also note Apple Silicon sometimes needs the okta-agent update (v1.3.2+) for stable utun handling.
Noah Kim: perfect, thanks! added a note to my onboarding checklist: "re-auth Okta + add temp 10.4/16 route if bastion unreachable; ensure okta-agent >=1.3.2 on M1/M2" :tada:
